reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

posts.text: Hafa Adai! Hawai’i and the other non-continent parts of our country have always hung together in Congress. In that spirit I welcomed Guam Delegate-Elect Alicia Anne Garrido Limtiaco to my office to kick off our partnership. Great addition to our ‘ohana! https://t.co/Die2LSQ5Ms

“Taste Korea, Taste Culture, Taste Kimchi!” Flew home for the weekend just ahead of the shutdown and joined the United Korean Assn of Hawaii’s 4th annual Kimchi Festival at Makiki Park (and made off with a stash of fresh kimchi). Gamsahamnida! https://t.co/QIIrEV4spz

Taste Korea, Taste Culture, Taste Kimchi!” Flew home for the weekend just ahead of the shutdown and joined the United Korean Assn of Hawaii’s 4th annual Kimchi Festival at Makiki Park (and made off with a stash of fresh kimchi). Gamsahamnida! https://t.co/1nSsjc6RDf

Here’s my next monthly Congressman Ed Case Reports on ‘Olelo Community Media, this one highlighting my district work including the Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP)/Hawai’i Chapter’s annual conference at the Japanese Cultural Center, the Pacific Islands Leadership Program at the East-West Center, the returning veterans of the Hawaiian Islands Honor Flight at HNL, and Aloha Tower’s Centennial Celebration: https://t.co/80WbyKQVLd

During the Iran war Hawai’i has needed the Jones Act waiver to keep fuel supplies flowing for our energy needs. I asked the President to again extend the waiver to continue assuring we get what we need while international energy supply chains are disrupted. But we shouldn’t have to beg for a waiver to start with to access cheaper domestic supplies which the Jones Act prevents. https://t.co/cZkyYUIOpA

I joined KHON2 Wake Up 2day yesterday to update on current veterans issues, the post-election landscape on Capitol Hill, my continued focus on affordability, Hegseth impeachment/Department of Defense oversight, completing current year appropriations and more. Here’s a replay: https://t.co/LYTz7cZobp
https://t.co/wLUh0Hfw1B

As a then-member of our House Natural Resources Committee, I worked for passage in ’20 of our landmark Great American Outdoors Act to reinvest in our national parks and other special public lands. This Congress I’m cosponsoring H.R. 9250, our America the Beautiful Act, to extend https://t.co/Cpx2I5xlMt
Back on Capitol Hill for the first time since the elections. Tons to do in the rest of the year. Here’s my quick report. https://t.co/64WLlSzLv2

The elections are over, but the challenges and work remain. Here’s my next Congressman Ed Case Reports districtwide enewsletter, “Closing Out The 119th Congress; Districtwide Survey Results; Your Thoughts”, for what’s on my agenda for the remaining two months of the current 119th https://t.co/D5CP1x3lV0

If you’re eligible to vote and haven’t already voted, please vote today. Ballots must be received by 7pm. Don’t mail your ballot; it won’t be received by then. Drop your ballot in one of 17 ballot drop boxes around O’ahu by 7pm. Vote in person at one of Oahu’s four Voter Services https://t.co/NNSK4GWSB2

I was honored to join the retirement ceremony aboard the USS Missouri of Lieutenant Colonel Kaiali’i Kahele from a distinguished twenty-five year career with the Hawai’i Air National Guard and United States Air Force Reserve, culminating as Senior Director, Air Mobility Division, https://t.co/4odaywi98M

An always-inspiring and educational day when I personally interview the best of our high school seniors seeking my annual nomination to our military service academies. Last week was no exception as I worked my way through 28 applicants and again concluded that our Hawai’i will continue to do us proud in our armed services.

I addressed the Hawai’i Chapter of the National Assn of Tax Professionals, the folks nationwide that help you make sense of your taxes, at their annual convention in Waikiki on national taxation issue before Congress as well as our individual constituent services on tax-related questions. More: https://t.co/0jkFr2aKmm.

When Congress comes back into session November 9thfor the remaining two months of the current 119th Congress, one of my top priorities will be to advance H.R. 10828, the Prohibit Corrupt Russia Oil Deals Act, bipartisan legislation I cosponsored to block the President’s https://t.co/OIZA9b3m9q

I joined Philippine Ambassador to the U.S. Jose Manuel Romualdez, Philippine Consul General Arman Talba and our Fil-Am community and others at the Philippine Consulate for a special showing of “Stories from the Field: Filipino Migrant Workers in Hawai’i”, a Smithsonian Asian https://t.co/aFmkVyWOvB

Here’s my next monthly Congressman Ed Case Reports on ‘Olelo Community Media, this one on: my House Appropriations Defense Subcommittee’s California field hearing on strengthening our industrial base; opening Mililani High’s federally-supported MEERS Lab to foster career paths in industrial trades; the We Are Kalihi celebration at Kalakaua Middle; and my Problem Solvers gerrymandering reform news conference from the Capitol. https://t.co/OFJ5WnHF6i

Individuals with disabilities should be able to access health insurance and services that do not force them out of their homes. The Latonya Reeves Freedom Act would ensure that states and long-term service and support insurance providers allow individuals with disabilities to https://t.co/3RcKyyrerw

One big consequence of our increasing natural disasters is the cost and availability of property insurance, and we have to pursue different paths to keep it available and affordable. I co-introduced the Community Disaster Protection Act to promote the development of new disaster https://t.co/xcmE6FXTaH

Hau’oli 100th La Hanau Aloha Tower! I was honored to join and provide thoughts at our iconic landmark’s centennial celebration and blessing ceremony as it reopened after major repairs, which I was able to partially fund through a $2 million direct Congressional Project Funding approval. I spoke of the history it has witnessed, the aloha it has emanated and the symbol it is for generations of kama’aina and visitors alike, as well as the need to continue to care for it for the generations coming.

I joined Gov. Green, Mayor Blangiardi, Hawai’i Public Housing Authority Exec. Dir. Hakim Ouansafi, and many partners in the dedication and grand opening of Ho’ohiki Senior Living on North School Street. These “250 new affordable senior homes in the heart of Honolulu” are not only a beautiful part of the answer to our affordable housing crisis but highlight the possibilities of committed public-private partnerships to meet other challenges.https://t.co/JNnwUvWXzc

Hawai‘i general election ballots are being mailed to all registered voters. For info on registering, registration status, voting (by mailing back, dropping in ballot box or in person), deadlines, assistance or other voting questions: https://t.co/5b9dyTIBXF https://t.co/RnJCXYc57d

I joined Hawaiian Islands Honor Flight at HNL in welcoming home 25 of our veterans – 24 Vietnam War and 1 Korean War – from a three-day trip to DC where they visited the Capitol, Arlington and our memorials. For most it was their first time in the capital of the country for which they fought. The great Honor Flight Network (https://t.co/L3gUYYOmSa) works nationally to “show our nation’s veterans the appreciation and honor they deserve” by providing a trip to DC to “share this momentous occasion with other comrades, remember the fallen, and share their stories and experiences with other veterans. Honored veterans always travel free of charge, thanks to generous donations to our organization” (including for our vets free airfare by Alaska/Hawaiian).

Franchising is a proven business approach that gives promising companies and products opportunities to grow (think L&L) and local owners opportunities to prosper (think McDonalds or 7-11). Today some 8.8 million jobs nationally are franchise-related, some 85% of franchisees live in their communities, and some 64% of franchisees are first-time business owners. Happy to join bipartisan colleagues in receiving the Franchise Champion Award for my support in Congress. https://t.co/fBXAd6c7tw

Working thru full week back home talking w/folks on various issues including: Laulani Teale on military presence in Hawai’i; Dr. Michael Carney on federal cancer research funding; Honolulu Museum of Art Director David Odo and Deputy Director Penni Hall on federal support possibilities; new Republic of Korea Consul General Sangmin Nam on US-Korea relations and assisting our Korean American community; and  AARP Hawaii’s Keali’I Lopez and Audrey Suga-Nakagawa on national kupuna issues.

I continue to be deeply honored to represent our Hawaii’s and country’s some 4.6 million Filipino Americans, and very proud to once again join my colleagues to commemorate this October as Filipino American History month. In doing so, we remember and honor the sacrifices and contributions of generations past and present, the embodiment of the best of America that Filipino Americans represent, and the continued advancement and promise of future generations. https://t.co/qhI4PNBXgp

Huge congrats to the University of Hawai’i- West O’ahu and to Pueo everywhere as you kick off your 50th Anniversary Celebration Week. UHWO has grown into such an integral part of our community and you have truly lived up to your mission of “empowering generations of learners.” Mahalo and here’s to many more generations to come. https://t.co/wwChRmITPj

Another Constituent Services Highlight on my office’s individual assistance: A constituent couldn’t get his deceased father’s Savings Bonds transferred over to his mother’s account. We contacted the U. S. Treasury Dept to get it done. More info on our services: https://t.co/0jkFr2aKmm

I joined the new bipartisan Congressional Free Enterprise Caucus, co-chaired by my colleagues Lou Correa and David Valadeo of California, August Pfluger of Texas and Brad Schneider of Illinois, and “dedicated to advancing public policy that strengthens free markets, restores fiscal discipline, and secures America's long-term economic leadership”. We can and must pursue integrated policies that are all of pro-growth, pro-worker and fiscally responsible. https://t.co/tExkN3tyuP

I join all of our Hawai‘i in remembering and honoring the life and legacy of U. S. Representative Patricia (Pat) Saiki.

She is rightly credited with many specific accomplishments. But above all she was a pioneer who broke barriers, easing the path for others that followed, and her decades of public service were marked by commitment to her country and Hawai‘i, determination, accomplishment, example and grace.

Rep. Saiki was a worthy steward of the office of Hawaii’s First Congressional District, setting a high bar for those that followed and will follow. I join in extending my sincere condolences and appreciation to her beloved family.
Mahalo to Evan Leong/Greater Good Radio for talking story about my journey to and through public service including my efforts in Congress. https://t.co/Gy3I967g9N

Voters deserve to know who specifically is funding political ads rather than secret spending behind deceptive fronts. I joined colleagues Reps Kevin Mullin (California) and Marcy Kaptur (Ohio) in introducing our Sunlight on SuperPACs Act, which would require federal campaign ads supported by SuperPACs (large-scale contributing fronts) to disclose their big donors. https://t.co/oYRTuigx5D

My @ProbSolveCaucus Gerrymandering Reform Working Group, which I co-chair, rolled out our package of four related congressional redistricting reform legislative proposals at a press conference from Capitol Hill. https://t.co/NQfyZkVnHl https://t.co/hnYNJrQCMX

It was an honor to welcome three of my partners, the Hons. Hirofumi Nakasone, Seiji Maehara and Akihisa Nagashima of the National Diet of Japan (Japan’s Congress) to Washington D.C. I took them on a personal tour of the Capitol as we discussed the importance of the U.S.-Japan alliance, our shared commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific, and continued support for Japan’s national security. Mahalo to our Japanese colleagues for visiting the Capitol, and for continuing to strengthen the enduring friendship between our nations and, especially, our Hawai’i.

Time again for my annual Congressional App Challenge open to middle and high school students in my district; October 26, 2026 submission deadline. The nationwide App Challenge in most congressional districts challenges our students to create an original app for a smartphone, tablet, or computer device about any topics using any programming language, with winners bringing their apps to Capitol Hill.  More info: https://t.co/h0KiM9l6Hu.

Congress considers the Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) every few years to authorize iwater resources: environmental, structural, navigational, flood protection, hydrology and related projects which the United States Army Corps of Engineers builds, so we spend a lot of effort getting needed Hawai’i projects into each WRDA. Great news that the House passed our latest WRDA with a bunch of my requests included, especially upgrading Honolulu Harbor. More: https://t.co/KnhzaUxZPl.

From-back-home DC meetings this week included one common theme; moving people and our stuff around and related federal issues: M. Dyer Global, a local employee-owned moving company, especially focusing on matters regarding moving our military families; and Mike Niethammer and Henry Aquino of the Hawai’i Automobile Dealers Association, moving all of us.

I always look forward to meeting with our Hawai’i veterans reps visiting DC, including this week Jame Schaedel of the Veterans of Foreign Wars/Hawai’i and (to his credit and Hawaii’s benefit) a member of VFW’s National Legislative Committee, here for VFW’s fall legislative conference. We discussed several VFW priorities; more here: https://t.co/1aHCPuhvq7$

As our national debt passes through $40 trillion, I joined the House Budget Committee for its field hearing in Dallas, TX on a critical issue: solutions to our federal fiscal/debt crisis. I am a co-introducer of several of the main measures before the Committee that provide a path forward. https://t.co/LewvzQLjHY

I joined colleague Rep. Jeff Hurd of Colorado on C-SPAN’s Ceasefire to discuss our Problem Solvers Caucus’ congressional redistricting/gerrymandering reform initiatives, AI regulation, the midterms and other subjects. https://t.co/DLg3hkckZW https://t.co/TGLC5VBFtO

Here’s my next monthly Congressman Ed Case Reports on ‘Olelo Community Media, this one of my recent district activities including the Filipino Chamber of Commerce’s Installation Banquet, Waipahu Soto Zen Temple’s Obon, Congressional Gold medal presentation to Jessica Lee, review of Hurricane Lala damage, and Okinawan Festival, as well as my DC remarks to the Asian Pacific American Institute for Congressional Studies Tech Summit on next-generation connectivity and digital equity. https://t.co/c3JDJbsaYq

My proposed legislation with Rep. Jim Moylan of Guam to strengthen federal efforts against destructive invasive species passed the full House on a vote of 371-33. This is especially important to our island homes, and especially in the wake of natural disasters to both Hawai’i and Guam which worsen the spreads of invasive species. More: https://t.co/BEOeFuJIGK

A very full week on Capitol Hill included a bunch of meetings with folks visiting from home, many with a community health/wellbeing focus, including: American Cancer Society Cancer Action Network; Network Enterprises Hawaii securing good employment for our disabled; Global Medical Response operating many of our ground and air ambulances; and Delta Dental/ Hawaii Dental Service.

Yesterday was my third full vote in the U.S. House to cease the Iran war without Congressional authorization. The vote grew to 220 for, 204 against. Time for the Senate to also fully assert Congress’ responsibility to decide when and how our country should go to war. https://t.co/IXHhXkz1N2

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
